mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with rising consumer confidence (HOUST) predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as stronger labor market momentum supports corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above its 12-month moving average while HOUST rises by at least 10% in the same month
failure_condition: In regimes with high inflation, the 60-day forward return is negative or no better than random chance ( IC < 0.05 ).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests weakening supply-side constraints, which tends to coincide with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as demand reallocation favors equities.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in a single month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in >70% of such events across 5-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative due to preemptive rate hike anticipation and reduced equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for at least 2 months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in >50% of such events over 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as risk aversion increases and equities are discounted for slower growth.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is non-negative in >70% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both employment (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as dual labor and demand drivers support earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA and HOUST > 12-month MA in the same month
regime_hint: Dual labor and consumer demand acceleration
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative in >40% of such events during non-recessionary periods.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 5% over three months suggests structural supply-side weakness, which tends to precede negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as risk premia rise.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% over 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (IC > 0.95) in 80% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4% and coincides with a sharp drop in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) by 1% in the same month, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is likely to be positive as the market anticipates easing and lower inflation.
candidate_trigger: 3-month MA of FEDFUNDS < 4% AND CPIAUCSL < 12-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in >60% of such events when inflation is sticky (>3% 6-month MA).
